headline: Seven in ten people now live where families have fewer than two children
why: Below-replacement fertility across most of the world points to the first sustained global population decline outside of plague and war.

headline: Warming is speeding up, and seven of Earth's sixteen vital signs hit records
why: A sevenfold faster warming rate than last century commits oceans and ice to changes that will keep unfolding long after anyone alive today.

headline: For the first time, people over 65 outnumber children under five worldwide
why: Humanity has always been young. An ageing species changes work, care, pensions, politics and growth in ways historians will treat as an era shift.

headline: An AI system disproves an 80-year-old Erdős geometry conjecture
why: Checked by outside mathematicians, it marks machines producing original mathematics, a capability that could change how all of science discovers things.

headline: Countries give themselves more time to finish the pandemic treaty's key annex
why: Until the pathogen-sharing annex is agreed, the Pandemic Agreement cannot take effect; how it lands decides who gets vaccines in the next pandemic.

headline: Renewables passed coal as the world's biggest power source in 2025
why: Coal has led electricity for over a century. Clean sources now cover all new demand, the likely turning point of the fossil age.

headline: Artemis II brings the first crew back from the Moon in over 50 years
why: After half a century, humans travelled farther from Earth than ever, reopening crewed deep space with the aim of staying rather than visiting.

headline: The United States completes its withdrawal from the WHO
source: US Department of Health and Human Services
why: The largest funder leaving forces the WHO to shrink and rethink, reshaping global health cooperation and outbreak response for years.

headline: The High Seas Treaty takes effect, covering half the planet's surface
why: For the first time, the ocean beyond national borders gets shared rules and marine protected areas, a framework meant to outlast generations.

headline: The EU AI Act, the first broad law on artificial intelligence, takes effect
why: Its rules phase in over several years and set a template other countries copy for how AI may be built and used.

headline: Germany switches off its last three nuclear reactors
why: Europe's largest economy completed its exit from nuclear power, leaning on renewables and gas through the energy transition.

headline: A fusion experiment releases more energy than its lasers put in
why: Seventy years of trying finally produced fusion ignition in a lab, the first proof that the Sun's power source can work on Earth.

headline: ChatGPT launches and puts conversational AI in everyone's hands
why: The moment AI that writes and reasons went mainstream. Work, learning and thinking began to change at a speed few technologies have matched.

headline: The world population passes 8 billion
why: A milestone near the peak: growth is slowing fast, and how we share resources at this scale shapes the century.

headline: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine
why: Europe's largest war since 1945 rewired energy supplies, defence spending and alliances across the continent for years.

headline: The James Webb Space Telescope launches
why: The most powerful telescope ever built, looking back to the first galaxies and into the air of distant planets.

headline: WHO recommends the first malaria vaccine for children
why: After a century of trying, a vaccine against the parasite that kills hundreds of thousands of children each year.

headline: A 90-year-old woman gets the first approved mRNA COVID vaccine
why: A vaccine built in under a year on a new mRNA platform, which now promises faster vaccines for many diseases.

headline: AlphaFold predicts how proteins fold, solving a 50-year problem
why: AI cracked a core puzzle of biology, a sign that machines will speed up science itself. Drug design is already changing.

headline: NASA's SOFIA finds water on the Moon's sunlit surface
why: Water is not only in permanently dark craters, making it easier for future crews to use what the Moon offers.

headline: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
why: A global shock that reshaped health systems, work and trust, and led to the first pandemic treaty negotiations.

headline: Astronomers capture the first image of a black hole
why: Something long only described by equations became visible, made possible by linking telescopes across the whole planet.

headline: The United Kingdom votes to leave the European Union
why: The first country to choose to leave the EU, setting off years of negotiation and reshaping trade, borders and politics in Europe.

headline: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol at Go, a game thought too intuitive for machines
why: Learning systems showed creativity people did not expect, the turning point that put deep learning at the centre of AI.

headline: LIGO detects gravitational waves from colliding black holes
why: A century after Einstein predicted them, humanity gained a new sense: hearing the universe through ripples in spacetime.

headline: Nearly every country adopts the Paris Agreement on climate
why: The first deal where almost all nations committed to cut emissions; its success or failure decides the climate of the coming centuries.

headline: WHO declares the West African Ebola epidemic a global emergency
why: The largest Ebola outbreak ever drove the first Ebola vaccine and changes in how the world funds and runs emergency response.

headline: CERN finds the Higgs boson, the last missing piece of physics' standard model
why: Confirms how particles get mass, completing the best theory of matter we have and setting the agenda for what lies beyond.

headline: Scientists show CRISPR can cut DNA at any chosen spot
why: A cheap, precise way to edit genes. It is already curing inherited disease and will reshape medicine and farming for generations.

headline: Earthquake and tsunami cause the Fukushima nuclear disaster
source: German Federal Office for the Safety of Nuclear Waste Management
why: It turned public opinion on nuclear power: Germany decided to close all its reactors, and Japan shut most of its fleet for years.

headline: NASA's LCROSS impact confirms water ice on the Moon
why: Water means drinking, breathing and rocket fuel. It turned the Moon from a place to visit into a place people might live.

headline: WHO declares the first flu pandemic in 40 years (H1N1)
why: A real-world test of pandemic plans that exposed gaps in vaccine access, lessons that shaped preparedness for a decade.

headline: Satoshi Nakamoto publishes the Bitcoin white paper
why: Money without a central bank became technically possible, starting a long experiment in how trust and value work online.

headline: Lehman Brothers collapses and the financial crisis goes global
why: The biggest bankruptcy in US history set off a recession, years of austerity and a lasting loss of trust in banks and governments.

headline: Apple introduces the iPhone
why: The internet moved into every pocket. Daily life, attention, politics and commerce reorganised around the smartphone.

headline: An Indian Ocean tsunami kills over 200,000 people
why: There was no warning system. The disaster led to one, and changed how coastal countries prepare for the next wave.

headline: The Human Genome Project finishes reading our DNA
why: The complete instruction set for a human, published for all. Personalised medicine and gene therapies build on this map.

headline: WHO issues a global alert about a new illness later named SARS
why: The first new pandemic threat of the century. It led to new international health rules and a playbook used in every outbreak since.

headline: Euro notes and coins go into circulation in twelve countries
why: More than 300 million people swapped their national money overnight, binding European economies together in daily life.

headline: IBM's Deep Blue beats world chess champion Garry Kasparov
why: The first time a machine beat the best human at a game of intellect, a marker on the road to today's AI.

headline: Astronomers find the first planet orbiting a Sun-like star
why: Planets turned out to be common around other stars. The question of whether we are alone moved from philosophy to observation.

headline: CERN releases the World Wide Web into the public domain
why: Giving the web away for free let anyone build on it. How humanity shares knowledge changed as much as with the printing press.

headline: The Berlin Wall falls
why: The Cold War's front line opened overnight. Europe's map, alliances and politics were redrawn for the rest of the century.

headline: Countries sign the Montreal Protocol to protect the ozone layer
why: The only treaty every country has ratified. It shows global action can fix a planetary problem; the ozone layer is on course to heal.

headline: The World Health Assembly declares smallpox eradicated
why: A disease that killed hundreds of millions was wiped out on purpose, the first time humans ended a plague rather than surviving it.

headline: Apollo 11 lands, and humans walk on the Moon
why: The first time living beings from Earth stood on another world. It will be remembered as long as there are people to remember.

headline: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
why: For the first time a person left Earth and came back, proving our species is not bound to one world.

headline: Charles Keeling starts measuring carbon dioxide on Mauna Loa
why: The longest record of the air we changed. The rise it tracks will set sea levels and climates for thousands of years.

headline: Sputnik 1 becomes the first human-made object in orbit
why: The first step off the planet. Whatever humanity becomes in space, its timeline starts with this beeping metal sphere.

headline: Watson and Crick publish the double helix structure of DNA
why: Knowing how life copies itself made genetics an engineering subject. Medicine, farming and evolution itself are now open to deliberate change.

headline: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
why: For the first time, the world agreed that every person has the same basic rights. Laws and constitutions everywhere still lean on it.

headline: The first nuclear explosion lights up the New Mexico desert
source: US Office of Scientific and Technical Information
why: Humanity gained the power to end itself. Every generation since lives with that choice, and the fallout layer marks the rocks for geologists far ahead.

headline: Alexander Fleming notices mould killing bacteria in a petri dish
why: Penicillin opened the antibiotic age, which roughly doubled how long people live; how we keep or lose it will shape medicine for millennia.
